## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document competes the analysis comparing Inflammatory markers CRP and IL-6 (measured by ELISA) and immune cells (measured by Flow cytometry).

### Function Sourcing

First the functions are all sourced
```{r Functions, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#To access the functions directory why must direct to the parent directory
setwd("../..")

#A list of the function files is pulled
function_files <- list.files(paste0(getwd(),"/Functions"), pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)
#Those functions are then sourced
lapply(function_files, source)
```


### Data Loading

We load all the data of interest

```{r data_load, echo=FALSE}
#All Metadata objects have been stored in one location
mic_sg_fun_objects <- readRDS("~/Zimbabwe-Cardiometabolic-Analysis/Data/R_Data/mic_sg_fun_objects.RDS")

#Metdata objects
  #base: all processed metadata 
  base <- mic_sg_fun_objects$base_with_sg_fun
  
#Previusly Determined confounders are loaded
conf_vars <- readRDS("~/Zimbabwe-Cardiometabolic-Analysis/Data/R_Data/conf_vars.RDS")

#Confounders
  #conf_vars_all: All confounders in one vector
  #conf_vars_HDL: Confounders of HDL
  #conf_vars_LDL: Confounders of LDL
  #conf_vars_Trig: Confounders of Trig
  #conf_vars_Glucose: Confounders of Glucose
  conf_vars_all <- conf_vars$conf_vars_all
  conf_vars_HDL <- conf_vars$conf_vars_HDL
  conf_vars_LDL <- conf_vars$conf_vars_LDL
  conf_vars_Trig <- conf_vars$conf_vars_Trig
  conf_vars_Glucose <- conf_vars$conf_vars_Glucose

```


### Functional Differences by HIV and Treatment Status

####Cross Sectional Differences
```{r}


met_lmer_data <- base

sg_col_sums <- colSums(met_lmer_data[,4:5273])

sg_prev <- c()
for (j in 4:5273) {
  prev_j <- length(which(met_lmer_data[,j]>0))
  sg_prev <- append(sg_prev, prev_j)                 
}
nonzero_sums <- which(sg_col_sums>0 & sg_prev>16)
#Immune cell populations are defined
sg_fun_vars <- colnames(met_lmer_data)[nonzero_sums+3]



## Cross Sectional Statistics

# Stats will be generated across groups (i.e. Cohort) using the gp_stat_sum function

# Statistics are performed on cohorts at different time points

sg_fun_stats_co <- gp_stat_sum(data=met_lmer_data,            #Data set specified
                            sub_vars="Week",      #Subset variable for stratification is selected
                            dep_vars=sg_fun_vars,    #Dependent variables are the sg_fun_vars previously defined
                            gp_var="Cohort",      #Group variable is cohort
                            normality= FALSE,     #Data has not been normalized so we are doing nonparametric tests
                            adj="bonferroni"      #p-value adjustment method is Bonferroni
                            )  


sg_fun_stats_co$padj[which(sg_fun_stats_co$group1!="HC" & sg_fun_stats_co$group2!="HC")] <- p.adjust(sg_fun_stats_co$`p-value`[which(sg_fun_stats_co$group1!="HC" & sg_fun_stats_co$group2!="HC")],method="fdr")

sg_fun_stats_co$padj[which(sg_fun_stats_co$group1!="Exp" & sg_fun_stats_co$group2!="Exp")] <- p.adjust(sg_fun_stats_co$`p-value`[which(sg_fun_stats_co$group1!="Exp" & sg_fun_stats_co$group2!="Exp")],method="fdr")

sg_fun_stats_co$padj[which(sg_fun_stats_co$group1!="Naïve" & sg_fun_stats_co$group2!="Naïve")] <- p.adjust(sg_fun_stats_co$`p-value`[which(sg_fun_stats_co$group1!="Naïve" & sg_fun_stats_co$group2!="Naïve")],method="fdr")


sg_fun_diff <- sg_fun_stats_co$Measure[which(sg_fun_stats_co$padj<0.05)]


```


####Linear mixed effects models HIV Treatment States
```{r}

#We generate an linear mixed effects model data set to inlcude results
sg_fun_lm_data <- expand.grid(c("HIV_Status","Treatment"),sg_fun_vars)

colnames(sg_fun_lm_data) <- c("Predictor","Outcome")
#We generate fields for the statistics
sg_fun_lm_data["pval"] <- NA
sg_fun_lm_data["padj"] <- NA
sg_fun_lm_data["coef"] <- NA
sg_fun_lm_data["sig"] <- NA

for (r in sg_fun_vars) {
  lm_data_r <- met_lmer_data[,c("HIV_Status","Treatment",r)] 
  colnames(lm_data_r)[3] <- "Outcome"
  lm_data_r$Outcome <- as.numeric(lm_data_r$Outcome)
  lm_r <- lm(Outcome~HIV_Status+Treatment, data=lm_data_r)
  sum_r <- summary(lm_r)
  HIV_p <- sum_r$coefficients[2,4]
  HIV_coef <- sum_r$coefficients[2,1]
  Trt_p <- sum_r$coefficients[3,4]
  Trt_coef  <- sum_r$coefficients[3,1]
  sg_fun_lm_data$pval[which(sg_fun_lm_data$Predictor=="HIV_Status" & sg_fun_lm_data$Outcome==r)] <- HIV_p
  sg_fun_lm_data$coef[which(sg_fun_lm_data$Predictor=="HIV_Status" & sg_fun_lm_data$Outcome==r)] <- HIV_coef
  sg_fun_lm_data$pval[which(sg_fun_lm_data$Predictor=="Treatment" & sg_fun_lm_data$Outcome==r)] <- Trt_p
  sg_fun_lm_data$coef[which(sg_fun_lm_data$Predictor=="Treatment" & sg_fun_lm_data$Outcome==r)] <- Trt_coef
}

sg_fun_lm_data$padj[which(sg_fun_lm_data$Predictor=="HIV_Status")] <- p.adjust(sg_fun_lm_data$pval[which(sg_fun_lm_data$Predictor=="HIV_Status")], method="fdr")

sg_fun_lm_data$padj[which(sg_fun_lm_data$Predictor=="Treatment")] <- p.adjust(sg_fun_lm_data$pval[which(sg_fun_lm_data$Predictor=="Treatment")], method="fdr")





```

####GSEA analysis
```{r}
library(clusterProfiler)

# Use the stat_rank (sign of coef * -log10 p-value) for a more robust ranking
# Filter for HIV_Status as an example
gene_list_hiv <- sg_fun_lm_data %>%
  filter(Predictor == "HIV_Status") %>%
  mutate(stat_rank = sign(coef) * -log10(pval)) %>%
  arrange(desc(stat_rank)) %>%
  # Pull the rank and name it with the KO ID
  { setNames(.$stat_rank, .$Outcome) }

# Remove any potential NA values
gene_list_hiv <- gene_list_hiv[!is.na(gene_list_hiv)]

# Run GSEA
gsea_results_hiv <- gseKEGG(geneList = gene_list_hiv,
                        organism = 'ko',
                        minGSSize = 10,
                        maxGSSize = 500,
                        pvalueCutoff = 1.0,
                        pAdjustMethod = "BH")

hiv_GSEA_result <- gsea_results_hiv@result %>%
  # Create a temporary column for absolute NES to sort by
  mutate(abs_NES = abs(NES)) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs_NES)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 20) %>%
  # Reorder the y-axis by the actual NES (not absolute) so they flow - to +
  mutate(Description = fct_reorder(Description, NES))

hiv_dotplot <- ggplot(hiv_GSEA_result, aes(x = NES, y = Description)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = setSize, color = p.adjust)) +
  # Use a gradient that highlights significance (low p-values)
  scale_color_continuous(low = "red", high = "blue", name = "p.adj") +
  # Adjust size range to make dots legible
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(3, 8), name = "Gene Count") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "HIV Enrichment Analysis",
    x = "NES",
    y = NULL,
    tag="A",
    color="p-adjusted"
  ) +
    theme(legend.position = "right",
          title = element_text(size = 20),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 15),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 15),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 15),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size=15),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 15),
        strip.text.x = element_text(size=12),
        strip.text.y = element_text(size=15),
        plot.tag = element_text(size=25),
        ggh4x.facet.nestline = element_blank(),
        strip.background.x = element_rect(
          color="black", fill="gray", linetype="solid"
        ),
        strip.background.y = element_rect(
          color="black", fill="gray", linetype="solid"
        ))+
  # Add a vertical line at 0 for easier interpretation of Up/Down regulation
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50")

#Now for treatment

# Use the stat_rank (sign of coef * -log10 p-value) for a more robust ranking
# Filter for HIV_Status as an example
gene_list_trt <- sg_fun_lm_data %>%
  filter(Predictor == "Treatment") %>%
  mutate(stat_rank = sign(coef) * -log10(pval)) %>%
  arrange(desc(stat_rank)) %>%

  { setNames(.$stat_rank, .$Outcome) }



# Remove any potential NA values
gene_list_trt <- gene_list_trt[!is.na(gene_list_trt)]

# Run GSEA

trt_dotplot <- ggplot(trt_GSEA_result, aes(x = NES, y = Description)) +
```

###Functional Differences by Metabolic Outcome

####Linear Mixed Effects Models  - All Participants

```{r}

#metaboic variables are defined
met_vars <- c("HDL","LDL","Trig","Glucose")
#We generate an linear mixed effects model data set to inlcude results
sg_fun_lm_met_data <- unique(expand.grid(sg_fun_vars, met_vars))

colnames(sg_fun_lm_met_data) <- c("Predictor","Outcome")
#We generate fields for the statistics
sg_fun_lm_met_data["pval"] <- NA
sg_fun_lm_met_data["padj"] <- NA
sg_fun_lm_met_data["coef"] <- NA
sg_fun_lm_met_data["sig"] <- NA
sg_fun_lm_met_data["percent_variance_exp"] <- NA

for (k in 1:nrow(sg_fun_lm_met_data)) {
  
  #Response variable is pulled out
  response <- as.character(sg_fun_lm_met_data$Outcome[k])
  
  #We pull the confounders for that variable
  conf_r_pre <- get(paste0("conf_vars_",response))
  
  conf_r <- setdiff(conf_r_pre,c("Location"))
  
  #Predictor variable is pulled out
  predictor <-  as.character(sg_fun_lm_met_data$Predictor[k])
  #We add the confounders with the predictor
  predictor_with_confs <- c(predictor,conf_r)

  #We remove missing variables
  data_r <- na.omit(met_lmer_data[,c(response,predictor_with_confs)])
  
  if (min(sapply(data_r, function(x) length(unique(x)))>1)) {
   # create full model 
  ff <- as.formula(paste0(response,"~",paste0(predictor_with_confs, collapse="+"))) 
  fm <- lm(ff,data = data_r)
  
  predict_fm <- predict(fm)
  sum_fm <- summary(fm)
  
  #Below we calculate the R -suared value
  #First total sum of squares
    tss <- sum((unlist(data_r[,c(response)])-mean(unlist(data_r[,c(response)])))^2)
    #Second residual sum of squares
    rss <- sum((unlist(data_r[,c(response)])-predict_fm)^2)
  #R-squared
  r_squared <- 1-(rss/tss)
  #Percent variance explained
  pve <- r_squared*100
  
  sg_fun_lm_met_data$percent_variance_exp[k] <- pve
  class(pve) <- "numeric"
  
  #We pull out the coefficinets
  coef_fm <- as.data.frame(sum_fm$coefficients)
  
  sg_fun_lm_met_data$pval[k] <- coef_fm[2,4]
  sg_fun_lm_met_data$coef[k] <- coef_fm[2,1] 
  }

  
  
}

for (m in met_vars) {
  
  sg_fun_lm_met_data$padj[which(sg_fun_lm_met_data$Outcome==m)] <- p.adjust(sg_fun_lm_met_data$pval[which(sg_fun_lm_met_data$Outcome==m)], method="fdr")
  
}




```

####Linear Mixed Effects Models  - Naive Participants
```{r}

#metaboic variables are defined
met_vars <- c("HDL","LDL","Trig","Glucose")
#We generate an linear mixed effects model data set to inlcude results
sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive <- unique(expand.grid(sg_fun_vars, met_vars))

colnames(sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive) <- c("Predictor","Outcome")
#We generate fields for the statistics
sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive["pval"] <- NA
sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive["padj"] <- NA
sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive["coef"] <- NA
sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive["sig"] <- NA
sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive["percent_variance_exp"] <- NA

for (k in 1:nrow(sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive)) {
  
  #Response variable is pulled out
  response <- as.character(sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive$Outcome[k])
  
  #We pull the confounders for that variable
  conf_r_pre <- get(paste0("conf_vars_",response))
  
  conf_r <- setdiff(conf_r_pre,c("HIV_Status","Treatment","Location"))
  
  #Predictor variable is pulled out
  predictor <-  as.character(sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive$Predictor[k])
  #We add the confounders with the predictor
  predictor_with_confs <- c(predictor,conf_r)
  
  #We remove missing variables
  data_r <- na.omit(met_lmer_data[which(met_lmer_data$Cohort=="Naïve"),c(response,predictor_with_confs)])
  
  if (min(sapply(data_r, function(x) length(unique(x)))>1)) {
    # create full model 
    ff <- as.formula(paste0(response,"~",paste0(predictor_with_confs, collapse="+"))) 
    fm <- lm(ff,data = data_r)
    
    predict_fm <- predict(fm)
    sum_fm <- summary(fm)
    
    #Below we calculate the R -suared value
    #First total sum of squares
    tss <- sum((unlist(data_r[,c(response)])-mean(unlist(data_r[,c(response)])))^2)
    #Second residual sum of squares
    rss <- sum((unlist(data_r[,c(response)])-predict_fm)^2)
    #R-squared
    r_squared <- 1-(rss/tss)
    #Percent variance explained
    pve <- r_squared*100
    
    sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive$percent_variance_exp[k] <- pve
    class(pve) <- "numeric"
    
    #We pull out the coefficinets
    coef_fm <- as.data.frame(sum_fm$coefficients)
    
    sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive$pval[k] <- coef_fm[2,4]
    sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive$coef[k] <- coef_fm[2,1] 
  }
  
  
  
}

for (m in met_vars) {
  
  sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive$padj[which(sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive$Outcome==m)] <- p.adjust(sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive$pval[which(sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive$Outcome==m)], method="fdr")
  
  assign(paste(m,"_sig_genes"), unique(sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive$Predictor[which(sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive$padj<0.05 & sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive$Outcome==m)]))
}

test_data <- met_lmer_data[which(met_lmer_data$Cohort=="Naïve"),]

test_lm_data <- sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive[which(sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive$Outcome=="LDL" & sg_fun_lm_met_data_naive$padj<0.05),]
```

```{r}
  # Add a vertical line at 0 for easier interpretation of Up/Down regulation
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50")


# Use the stat_rank (sign of coef * -log10 p-value) for a more robust ranking
# Filter for HIV_Status as an example
gene_list_trig <- sg_fun_lm_met_data %>%
  filter(Outcome == "Trig") %>%
  mutate(stat_rank = sign(coef) * -log10(pval)) %>%
  arrange(desc(stat_rank)) %>%
  # Pull the rank and name it with the KO ID
  { setNames(.$stat_rank, .$Predictor) }

# Remove any potential NA values
gene_list_trig <- gene_list_trig[!is.na(gene_list_trig)]

# Run GSEA
gsea_results_trig <- gseKEGG(geneList = gene_list_trig,
                            organism = 'ko',
                            minGSSize = 10,
                            maxGSSize = 500,
                            pvalueCutoff = 1.0,
                            pAdjustMethod = "BH")

trig_GSEA_result <- gsea_results_trig@result %>%
  # Create a temporary column for absolute NES to sort by
  mutate(abs_NES = abs(NES)) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs_NES)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 20) %>%
  # Reorder the y-axis by the actual NES (not absolute) so they flow - to +
  mutate(Description = fct_reorder(Description, NES))

trig_dotplot <- ggplot(trig_GSEA_result, aes(x = NES, y = Description)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = setSize, color = p.adjust)) +
  # Use a gradient that highlights significance (low p-values)
  scale_color_continuous(low = "red", high = "blue", name = "p.adj") +
  # Adjust size range to make dots legible
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(3, 8), name = "Gene Count") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Triglycerides Enrichment Analysis",
    x = "NES",
    y = NULL,
    tag="C",
    color="p-adjusted"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        title = element_text(size = 20),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 15),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 15),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 15),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size=15),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 15),
        strip.text.x = element_text(size=12),
        strip.text.y = element_text(size=15),
        plot.tag = element_text(size=25),
        ggh4x.facet.nestline = element_blank(),
        strip.background.x = element_rect(
          color="black", fill="gray", linetype="solid"
        ),
        strip.background.y = element_rect(
          color="black", fill="gray", linetype="solid"
        ))+
  # Add a vertical line at 0 for easier interpretation of Up/Down regulation
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50")
```
